claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic FeCoNiCrMn.
The annealed initial alloy has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
Aging at 600 °C for 12 h will induce approximately 5 vol % coherent Laves-type Fe2Ni precipitates.
The precipitates induced by aging will have an average size of approximately 5 nm.
The matrix composition will remain unchanged after precipitation.
The hypothesis holds for coherent precipitate fractions of 2–10 vol % and sizes of 2–20 nm.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates act as low-energy nucleation sites for a field-driven magnetic phase transition.
The precipitates lower the energy barrier for the field-driven magnetic phase transition.
The precipitates reduce magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Phonon scattering at coherent precipitate interfaces accelerates heat transfer.
Precipitate coherency preserves mechanical integrity.
Precipitate coherency minimizes thermal hysteresis.
Aging will increase magnetic entropy change at 0.5–1 T by 2–3 J kg^-1 K^-1 relative to the unaged alloy.
Aging will reduce thermal hysteresis by more than 0.5 K.
The aged alloy's thermal conductivity will remain within 10% of the baseline.
Aging will increase yield strength by approximately 10%.
The unaged alloy has a magnetic entropy change of approximately 2 J kg^-1 K^-1 at 1 T.
The unaged alloy has thermal hysteresis of approximately 1 K.
The unaged alloy has thermal conductivity of approximately 12 W m^-1 K^-1.
The unaged alloy has yield strength of approximately 400 MPa.

contradictions.description: In a closed equiatomic alloy, forming approximately 5 vol % Fe2Ni precipitates necessarily partitions Fe and Ni and therefore changes the residual matrix composition; the intervention simultaneously asserts precipitate formation and an unchanged matrix composition without specifying external solute addition or another mass-balance mechanism.

The proposed rapid-heat-exchange mechanism relies on enhanced phonon scattering, which is not coherently connected to faster heat transport and sits uneasily with the prediction that thermal conductivity will be maintained. No separate interfacial heat-transfer metric or explanation resolving this tension is provided.
